newsitem.title: JAPAN: Conditions favour rise in Japan net exports -- BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Conditions favour rise in Japan net exports -- BOJ.

text.p: Economic conditions in Japan and abroad still favour a rise in Japan's net exports, a Bank of Japan (BOJ) official told a news conference on Thursday.
"Conditions which favour a rise in (Japan's) exports still prevail," said Masayuki Matsushima, director of the BOJ's Research and Statistics Department.

He said healthy overseas demand and a weakening of the yen until this spring were behind the rise in exports. He added that although the yen had strengthened recently, its exchange rate to the dollar was at similar levels to 1991.
He said Japanese goods had regained competitiveness due to the weak yen after their competitiveness decreased in 1994 and 1995.
He said Japan's current account surplus was likely to move steadily along with net exports following a significant rise in the April-to-June period.
